solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Items of underwear? They can provide uplift

definitions.meaning: warm long underclothes worn in cold weather
rising currents of warm air that lift gliders and birds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplift' teases the reader towards a supportive undergarment, but the second sense is meteorological.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is warm winter underclothing; the other is rising columns of heated air, and the bra-like 'uplift' joke links them.

clue.text: New track made, being this?

indicators.note: something new is freshly made over, so these two words are rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A freshly laid road surface, asking what state it is now in.
explanation.definitionFit: A road newly surfaced with asphalt has been given its black coating, which is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Suffers endless rudeness unfortunately

indicators.note: something that turns out unfortunately has gone awry, so the shortened word is jumbled
without an end, so the word rudeness loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with constant rudeness, which is unfortunate for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last S of RUDENESS, leaving RUDENES, and 'unfortunately' jumbles that.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer something is to bear or tolerate it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Somewhere in India that is a source of irritation for me

parts.note: belonging to me is my
a sore is a painful, irritated spot

explanation.surface: A traveller complains that a particular Indian place annoys them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysore is a city in the state of Karnataka in southern India.

clue.text: It brings something extra into view, liberal portion

definitions.text: It brings something extra into view

parts.note: a ration is an allotted portion

explanation.surface: A generous serving that adds something extra to what you see.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds vague but is astronomical: the Moon's slight wobble lets us see a little more than half its surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moon's apparent oscillation reveals extra parts of its surface to Earth observers, technically bringing more into view.

clue.text: Try to stop others going to best film

definitions.text: Try to stop others going to

parts.note: the pick of a group is its best
ET is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone tries to keep others away from the finest film showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikers stand at a workplace gate to deter others from entering, a verb sense of blockading.

clue.text: Greek character nicked a coin once

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
nicked is British slang for stole

explanation.surface: A Greek person stole an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistole was an old gold coin, chiefly Spanish, no longer in circulation.

clue.text: Set of notes showing what to put in baby's bed

definitions.meaning: a crib is a set of illicit notes used in an exam

definitions.text: what to put in baby's bed
definitions.meaning: linen laid in a cot, or crib

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is concealed exam notes; read literally, it is bedding for an infant's cot.

clue.text: Mythological female chosen to accompany sun god

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in president-elect
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A legendary woman is selected to go alongside a solar deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is the daughter of Agamemnon in Greek legend, avenging his murder.

clue.text: Wine — have some more, dear

indicators.note: some of the words gives a run of their letters, here across the comma

explanation.surface: A host offers a guest another glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is short for red wine, a common shortening.

clue.text: Editor, having got the message, resigned

parts.note: a sub, or subeditor, edits copy
a missive is a letter or message

explanation.surface: An editor quit after receiving a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resigned' looks like quitting a job, but it means accepting meekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resigned means passively accepting things, as a docile, yielding person does.

clue.text: Farmland's managed to accommodate one east of Indian city

definitions.note: the possessive acts as an adjective: of or relating to farmland

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means placed to the right of, so after

parts.note: Agra is the city of the Taj Mahal

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Farmland has been run so as to house someone east of an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian describes land and its cultivation, so it means 'of farmland'.

clue.text: Attacks with stones being thrown

indicators.note: thrown stones scatter, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Assaults carried out by throwing rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Onsets are assaults or charges, an old military sense of the word.

clue.text: Chest with equipment outside front of shop

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, here the gear around the letter

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A chest with gear standing outside a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Kist is a Scottish and northern word for a box or trunk.

clue.text: Exceptional rector in front of Welshmen — his voice carries

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unusual order
the front of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An outstanding clergyman preaching to Welsh men with a voice that carries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptional' rearranges RECTOR, IN and W from 'front of Welshmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellman made public announcements in the street, so a loud, carrying voice was his job.

clue.text: Asset with mice around? Install a moggy

indicators.note: to install is to put something in place inside, so the letter goes within the jumble
letters thrown around are scattered, so the pool is rearranged

explanation.surface: With mice running about, someone suggests getting a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' jumbles the first two clue words into SIMESECAT (or similar), and 'Install' then slots the A in to complete the breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A moggy is British slang for a cat; the Siamese is one particular breed.

clue.text: Mum's story about copper being virile

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters go round the metal

parts.note: ma is mum, plus the possessive s
a line is a story told to persuade, as in shoot a line
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Mother's tale of a policeman being manly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile means having strong manly qualities, a near synonym.

clue.text: Terrible grot eaten — something detrimental in early stages of life

definitions.text: something detrimental in early stages of life

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so these letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Eating awful filth harms you early in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grot' is British slang for rubbish or dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A teratogen is an agent that causes malformation of an embryo or foetus.

clue.text: Is message swirling around head bringing fatigue?

indicators.note: swirling around turns the first two pieces back to front

parts.note: word can mean a message, as in send word
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A confusing message spinning in someone's head makes them tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the head round which the message swirls, but it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsiness is sleepiness, a close match for tiredness.

clue.text: Rubbish lines being penned on work desk

indicators.note: penned means shut in a pen, so the outer word encloses the other

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
L is short for line, doubled for lines
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone writes poor verses while working at a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' suggests writing, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolltop is a desk whose writing surface is covered by a sliding slatted lid.

clue.text: Like some coffee, brown, in odd tins

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other
odd means strange, so the letters come out in a peculiar order

parts.note: tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: Brown coffee granules sold in unusual tins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges the container word into INST, which then holds the colour, splitting it as INS...T.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant coffee is made from soluble granules or powder, one kind among many.

clue.text: Beam from sailor embracing bishop

indicators.note: embracing means holding around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A sailor with a big smile hugging a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' reads as a smile, but it is a girder.
explanation.definitionFit: A girder with a T-shaped cross-section is one kind of structural beam.

clue.text: The rest going ahead of the Queen, a smashing person

indicators.note: going ahead means placed in front, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a break is a rest or pause
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Everyone else goes before the monarch, who is a splendid person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' looks like British slang for wonderful, but it means one who breaks things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shatters things is literally a smasher, so the definition reads cryptically.

clue.text: Stand-in fellow about to take precedence

indicators.note: to take precedence is to go first, so this piece leads

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a gent is a gentleman or fellow

explanation.surface: A substitute man who wants to be ahead of others.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules on behalf of a monarch who cannot, acting as a substitute.

clue.text: Female defeats jerks

parts.note: licks means beats or defeats

explanation.surface: A woman beats some idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' looks like idiots, but it is a verb, twitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Flicks and jerks both mean sudden sharp movements of the hand.

clue.text: It being most peaceful, that is time to get into search

indicators.note: to get into is to enter, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: a quest is a search
ie stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: It is calmest when it's time to begin a search.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of quiet means calmest, matching the definition exactly.

clue.text: Like a three-piece suit? New attire may be acquired after journey

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the other

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: New clothing might be bought after a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a suit in three parts, jacket, trousers and waistcoat, as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripartite means in three parts, which a three-piece outfit is.

clue.text: The ultimate in drink, say — one type of beer

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: The best of drinks, for instance a particular beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Keg beer is pasteurised, pressurised beer served from a metal cask.

clue.text: Expectorate having drunk Irish whiskey?

indicators.note: having drunk means having taken in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to expectorate is to spit

explanation.surface: Someone spits after drinking Irish whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskey is an example of a distilled alcoholic liquor, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Three bits missing from end of fifth book or two very small bits?

indicators.text: Three bits missing from end of
indicators.note: three letters are missing from the end of the book's name

parts.note: Deuteronomy is the fifth book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A riddle about a damaged book of scripture or tiny particles.
explanation.definitionFit: A deuteron is the nucleus of deuterium, a proton plus a neutron: two tiny particles.
